kripalu.cha1: O mind, worship the gracious Śrī Rāmacandra, who takes away the dreadful fear of worldly existence. His eyes are like fresh lotuses; his face, his hands and his red feet are lotuses too. ॥1॥
kripalu.cha2: His boundless beauty outshines countless Kāmadevas; he is lovely as a fresh dark rain cloud. His yellow garment gleams like pure lightning. I bow to him, the husband of Janaka's daughter. ॥2॥
kripalu.cha3: Worship him, the friend of the lowly, radiant as the sun, destroyer of the lines of the demons; the joy of Raghu's house, the root of bliss, the moon of Kosala, the son of Daśaratha. ॥3॥
kripalu.cha4: A crown on his head, earrings, a tilaka on his brow; his fair, noble limbs adorned with ornaments. His arms reach to his knees; he bears bow and arrows, and conquered Khara and Dūṣaṇa in battle. ॥4॥
kripalu.cha5: Thus says Tulasīdāsa: O delight of the minds of Śaṅkara, Śeṣa and the sages, destroyer of the host of the wicked, lust and the rest, make your home in the lotus of my heart. ॥5॥
bal.236.cha1: The one your heart is set on, that bridegroom, lovely by nature and dark, shall be yours; a treasury of compassion and all-wise, he knows your goodness and your love. Hearing Gaurī's blessing in these words, Sītā and her friends rejoiced at heart. Tulasīdāsa says: worshipping Bhavānī again and again, Sītā set off for the palace with a glad heart. ॥1॥
bal.236.so236: Knowing Gaurī to be gracious to her, Sītā felt a joy in her heart beyond telling; her left limbs, the root of fair good fortune, began to throb. ॥236॥
